_comment: Which live Meta campaigns the budget ladder drives, and which ones it is deliberately leaving alone. Read by scripts/budget-ladder.js; written by hand. This file exists because the ladder used to hold its campaign list as a hardcoded array in scripts/meta-budget-ladder.js, so a second event was a code edit -- and the edit nobody made was invisible, because a campaign missing from the array is simply never laddered. Adding an October event is now: add the event to brand.json, build the campaign, add four lines here.
_how_to_add: 1. The event must exist in content/brand.json under `events` -- the ladder reads its DATE from there and refuses a key it cannot find. Nothing about the ladder duplicates the event.
2. Decide legacy or v2 (see _fields.playbook below -- v2 is the current playbook for any event that doesn't already have a live campaign built on the legacy shape).

LEGACY (one campaign): build it (paused is fine) and take its numeric id from Ads Manager or `node scripts/meta-ads-review.js`. Add one entry: event, campaign_id, name, total (whole-run dollars), runway_start.

V2 (three campaigns): `node scripts/build-paid-campaign.js --event=<KEY> --execute` builds `<Event> | Cold`, `<Event> | 2-for-1` and `<Event> | Retargeting`, paused, budget on each campaign, per content/brand.json paid_template.playbook_v2. Add THREE entries, one per role, sharing the SAME `total` and `runway_start` -- each carries `playbook: "v2"` and `role: "cold"`, `"two_for_one"` or `"retargeting"`. The ladder carves the 2-for-1 share out of cold ONLY once the two_for_one entry exists; a pair without one (Loxleys) keeps the full cold rate. Do not set `share`; v2 does not use it (see _fields.playbook).
3. `node scripts/meta-budget-ladder.js --all` (dry run) and read the plan. `--forecast=45` shows what the account spends per day once the runs overlap.
4. Nothing else. The 03:00 `SparkDate Budget Ladder` scheduled task already runs `--all --execute`.

_fields.event: Key in content/brand.json events. The ladder gets the event date from there and nowhere else.
_fields.campaign_id: Numeric Meta campaign id. Legacy or v2, it must be a campaign with a campaign-level daily_budget (one ad set under it) -- the ladder sets that field and refuses a campaign that has none. The sentence that used to be here, 'v2 campaigns are ABO', was wrong: scripts/build-paid-campaign.js read it literally, put budgets on ad sets, and built campaigns the ladder could never touch. Corrected 2026-09-10 (playbook_v2.campaign.budget).
_fields.name: For output only. The live name is read back from Meta and printed next to it.
_fields.total: Whole-run budget in dollars, same meaning for both playbooks. Legacy: distributed across phases by percentage. v2: scales every phase's fixed per-day rate by total/296 (296 is the playbook's own reference event) -- a v2 event's cold AND retargeting entries both carry the SAME total, since it describes one shared run, not two independent budgets. Under $200 on legacy, prime falls below Meta's $2.00/day floor; validation warns. v2 has its own floor handling per phase (playbook_v2._floor_priority_rule) and does not need this warning.
_fields.runway_start: First day of spend. Legacy: must leave at least 18 days before the event (brand.json runway._floor) and ideally 21 (runway.minimum_days) -- prime literally disappears below the floor. v2: no hard floor -- a short runway gracefully starts later in the phase sequence instead (playbook_v2._lead_time.cold_start_rule), down to just Close's own window.
_fields.playbook: Optional, default legacy (i.e. omit this field). "v2" reads content/brand.json paid_template.playbook_v2 instead of the legacy campaign/ad_sets/phases -- see that block's own _comment. Existing entries (Loxleys) must never set this; its live campaign runs on legacy and changing this field would silently recompute a different rate for money already spending.
_fields.role: REQUIRED when playbook is "v2", and meaningless otherwise. "cold", "two_for_one" or "retargeting" -- which of the event's v2 campaigns this entry drives. One of each per event. two_for_one is the women-locked `<Event> | 2-for-1` campaign (playbook_v2._gender_rule), and its PRESENCE is what makes the ladder carve two_for_one_of_cold out of the cold rate -- register it and the cold entry drops by that share the same night.
_fields.share: Legacy only. Optional, default 1. The fraction of `total` THIS campaign carries, for a legacy event split across more than one campaign. Shares for one event may not sum above 1. v2 does NOT use this field -- its cold:retarget split varies BY PHASE (80/20 in Seed, 60/40 in Build, 35/65 in Close), which a single flat fraction cannot express; use `role` instead.
_fields.managed: Optional, default true. false parks an entry without deleting the numbers -- it keeps its id out of the ungoverned report while the ladder leaves it alone.
_fields.note: Why this entry is the way it is.

guards._why_account: Each ladder is individually sane at $11.57/day; four at once is the number nobody was watching. reports/OCTOBER_SLATE_FEASIBILITY_2026-09-03.md models the October slate peaking at $27.50-$32.50/day across four campaigns, and the account's real record is $24.67/day across the seven days to Sep 1. $40 clears the modelled peak and still catches a doubling. A breach refuses the WHOLE run rather than laddering some campaigns and not others.
guards._why_campaign: A ceiling, not a jump limit. The ladder's own prime -> convert step is 4.5x by design, so any jump guard tight enough to catch a typo also blocks the real steps. What needs catching is a fat-fingered total or a wrong event date, and both show up as an absurd daily figure.

campaigns.name: Loxleys | Sales
campaigns.note: MIGRATED to playbook v2 on 2026-09-08, when Loxleys' retargeting leg finally had an audience and an ad and could take its share. The $180 total is unchanged -- it is Taylor's $3.00/day prime choice on the original Traffic campaign (memory lx-campaign-live), carried onto the Sales campaign that replaced it on 09-05. What changes is the split: this campaign drops from the legacy convert rate of $9.00/day to v2's Build rate of $5.11, and the retargeting entry below takes $3.40. Total remaining across both legs is LESS than the legacy ladder's remaining, not more. Retire both entries after 2026-09-22.

campaigns.name: Loxley's Retargeting
campaigns.note: Same run, same total as the cold entry above -- v2 entries share one budget and split it BY PHASE (see _fields.total). Empty shell from 2026-08-17 until 2026-09-08, when it got both audiences, lost an inherited relationship_statuses filter costing ~78% of reach, and gained its first ad (LX-RT-PATIO). reports/LOXLEYS_RETARGETING_LAUNCH_2026-09-08.md is the whole story.

acknowledged.name: Marion Court | Sales
acknowledged.why: Hand-set to $14.00/day by Taylor. Built 09-05 as a T-3 hail mary on the 2-for-1 female creative; its budget is a deliberate flat push, not a ladder. Handing it to the ladder would pull it DOWN to the close-phase rate two days before the event.

acknowledged.name: Marion Court Retargeting
acknowledged.why: Left untouched on purpose (HANDOFF 09-05): MC-RT-QUANG and MC-RT-NO-SCORECARDS stay running for the data. $6/day, ends with the event.

_acknowledged_note: A campaign here is one that is ACTIVE and deliberately outside the ladder. Anything ACTIVE in the account that is in neither list is reported as UNGOVERNED and exits non-zero -- that is the whole point of the file. `review_after` makes an acknowledgement expire instead of muting a campaign forever.
_playbook_ref: reports/ADS_OBJECTIVE_GAP_ANALYSIS_2026-09-06.md section 8 is the current spec for a future event's phase structure (Seed/Build/Close), its cold:retarget split per phase, and its gender rule (rewritten 2026-09-10: ONE women-locked `<Event> | 2-for-1` campaign, role two_for_one here, everything else broad) -- built and offline-tested 2026-09-06 as content/brand.json paid_template.playbook_v2 and scripts/budget-ladder.js's roleRates()/phaseWindowsV2()/rateFor() dispatch (tests/budget-ladder.test.js, 22 cases). CORRECTION to what this note said when first written: it claimed the `share` field already covered a Cold+Retargeting split with no arithmetic change needed. That was wrong -- `share` is one flat fraction applied to every phase alike, and the playbook's cold:retarget ratio VARIES by phase (80/20 -> 60/40 -> 35/65), which a flat fraction cannot express. v2 entries use `role` ("cold"/"retargeting") instead of `share` -- see _fields.playbook and _fields.role above. UPDATE, same day: `node scripts/build-paid-campaign.js --event=<KEY> --execute` now builds this shape directly -- three PAUSED campaigns (Cold, 2-for-1, Retargeting), budget on each campaign, one ad set each, read-back verified against the account's own proven OUTCOME_SALES field values. Taylor, verbatim: "I don't want to retain the old shape, I want the new playbook for go forward" -- the script no longer knows how to build anything else. Loxleys' single entry above stays on legacy regardless -- rebuilding a LIVE campaign's structure this close to its 2026-09-22 event risks a cold-start at the worst time (playbook_v2._lead_time's own compressed-schedule rule), and it retires on its own in two weeks. The legacy campaign/ad_sets/phases fields in paid_template exist ONLY so scripts/budget-ladder.js can keep computing Loxleys' nightly rate until then -- they are wind-down, not a second supported shape, and are safe to delete once that entry retires.
